# Step 10: Power transformer black leads to fuse post and switch

> *Dress the power transformer black leads around the end bell and connect one lead to lug A of the fuse post (S). Connect other black lead to lug #1 of on-off switch (S).*

!!! info "Explainer pending"

*Topics to cover when written:*

- These are the [PA-060](../../components/pa-060-power-transformer.md) primary leads (120V AC mains side).
- Why the fuse goes in series with the primary — limiting fault current from the wall, protecting the transformer and the building wiring.
- How the on-off switch breaks the primary circuit — switching on the low-voltage side rather than after the transformer keeps the secondary completely de-energized when off.
- Why we route around the end bell (mechanical and shielding reasons).
- The [3-prong cord modification](../../modifications/3-prong-cord.md) intersection: the primary side is where the earth ground from the IEC cord lands, and we want the primary leads, fuse, and switch all in the same general area to keep the mains routing tight.
- The [anti-click cap modification](../../modifications/anti-click-cap.md): why an RC snubber across the switch eliminates the loud "pop" on power-off.
